messages.text:
"Create a REAL PLAYABLE 3D dark fantasy RPG for mobile, titled REGION ZERO. This must be a true 3D game with actual 3D geometry, meshes, terrain, lighting, depth, perspective and a controllable character. NOT 2D, NOT isometric, NOT a slideshow and NOT a text-only adventure.

GAMEPLAY: Third-person over-the-shoulder camera following a female protagonist with long dark hair and a small white streak. Touch joystick to walk, swipe to rotate camera, action button to interact. Smooth camera movement and collision detection. Mobile-optimized graphics and responsive controls.

WORLD: One small but richly detailed explorable ancient swamp and forest. Twisted trees, dense mist, wet soil, shallow water, crumbling stone ruins, pale moths and mysterious carvings. Gothic ancestral cosmic horror, haunting atmosphere, muted green, charcoal, purple and moonlight. Atmospheric lighting, environmental audio and ambient particles if possible.

INTERACTIONS: The player can freely walk around, examine a carved monolith, investigate a forgotten relic, follow two paths and talk to an enigmatic old woman. Interactive objects must trigger readable Spanish dialogue. Include meaningful dialogue choices and at least one choice that changes a later event. Add a small inventory and a simple hidden skill check. Keep the story mysterious; do not explain the origin of the world.

GOAL: Make a SHORT COMPLETE PLAYABLE VERTICAL SLICE. The player wakes up in the swamp, explores, discovers a clue, meets the old woman, makes a decision and reaches one of two different endings. Include start, gameplay and ending screens. Prioritize real 3D movement and working interactions over scope. All player-facing text must be in Spanish. If advanced graphics are not possible, use simple low-poly 3D assets but preserve genuine 3D exploration. (3D Game, Phone/Tablet)

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

1: ## Process lifecycle
2: 
3: - Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
5: - After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.
6: 
7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.
18: 
19: ## Mobile browser games
20: 
21: - Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
22: - Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
23: - Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
24: - Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

content.text:
Built **REGION ZERO** as a playable 3D browser game in `index.html`. It includes a third-person player, mobile joystick and swipe camera controls, a foggy swamp with 3D ruins and trees, Spanish interactions, an inventory, a choice that changes the ending, and start and ending screens.

To play, serve the project directory and open it in a browser. I checked the JavaScript syntax; I couldn’t verify the game in-browser because Chromium isn’t installed in this environment. Assumption: the game should run as a self-contained web page, loading Three.js from a CDN.
